title: [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois..., pages 650 bis à 787, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: in the unpublished continuation of La Longue Marche, Grothendieck studies a group scheme Z_{ρσ} over a base S. It is a schematic replacement for the group of automorphisms u of an extension 𝔖 attached to the modular group, presented by an order-3 generator ρ and an order-2 generator σ, coupled with a unit μ in a group scheme O*_12. The rank-2 lattice M = Zλ0 ⊕ Zλ1 carries actions ρ_M, σ_M. Inside it sits a sublattice M_0, with associated vector group M_0 (M_0 ⊗ G_a, in the underlined notation). The pair (u, μ) is encoded by the 'heads' ξ0 and η0 in M_0 via (135). The 'équation des têtes' is ξ0 = η0 + 3ν''(μ)λ1. Condition (136) says that ξ0 and η0 lie locally in the images of (1-ρ_M) and (1-σ_M).

On this page, using the previous page's computation (1-σ_M): M → Z ≅ G_a → M_0, λ ↦ λδ with δ = λ1 - λ0, Grothendieck observes the following. (136) reduces to a condition on η0 alone: (136 bis) η0 ∈ Im(G_a → M_0, λ ↦ λδ), which he identifies with Ker(M_0 → G_a, c0λ0 + c1λ1 ↦ c0 + c1).

He then records the basis (138): M_0 = Zδ ⊕ Z(3λ1), with 3λ1 = (1-ρ)δ, and correspondingly M_0 = G_a δ × G_a·(3λ1). Hence (139): Σ^{ff}_{ρ,σ} ≅ O*_12 × G_aδ via (μ, ξ0, η0) ↦ (μ, η0). This works because ξ0 is recovered from μ and η0 by the equation of heads, ξ0 = η0 + ν''(μ)·3λ1 (a crossed-out attempt wrote ξ0 via (1-ρ_M)^{-1}).

NB (converse parametrization): given ξ0 alone, the decomposition (138) yields η0 (the δ-coordinate) and ν'' (the 3λ1-coordinate). If ν2 and ν3 are also known, one gets 2ν0, using the next page's relation ν'' + ν2 - ν3 + 2ν2ν3 = 2ν0. Assuming 2 is a regular section of O_S, this gives ν0 and hence μ. This leads, on the next page, to the embedding (140) Σ ↪ M_0 × {0,1} × {0,1} when 2 is invertible, and to the extension 1 → G_a → Z_{ρσ} → O*_12 → 1 with Z_{ρσ} smooth of relative dimension 2.

Purpose: to compute explicitly the structure (smoothness, dimension, extension by G_a) of a centralizer/automorphism group scheme in a schematic version of the genus 0/1 Teichmüller-tower analysis.
errors: The identification Im(G_a → M_0, λ ↦ λδ) = Ker(M_0 → G_a, c0λ0 + c1λ1 ↦ c0 + c1) holds only when 3 is invertible on S, or when the map is read correctly. In the basis (138), δ ↦ 0 but 3λ1 ↦ 3, so the kernel is G_aδ × (3-torsion of G_a)·3λ1. Over a base where 3 is not invertible, the kernel strictly contains the image. Either the intended map differs, or a hypothesis (3 invertible, or S flat over Z) is implicit.

Lines are heavily crossed out. The surviving line '= ν''δ + ...' for ξ0 looks inconsistent with the equation of heads ξ0 = η0 + ν''(3λ1); it is likely an abandoned attempt rather than the final formula.
The converse recovery of μ needs 2 to be a non-zero-divisor (the NB) and is only made an embedding when 2 is invertible (next page). The page itself leaves the general-base case open.

ideas.what: Reduction of the local-image conditions (136) to a single linear condition on η0 using an explicit Z-basis of M_0.
ideas.modern_name: explicit computation of a vector-group-valued cocycle/coboundary condition

ideas.what: Identification of a centralizer-type group scheme Σ ≅ O*_12 × G_a (an extension of a finite-type unit group by G_a) attached to automorphisms of an SL2(Z)/braid-type extension, over an arbitrary base S.
ideas.modern_name: integral/schematic model of automorphism groups of modular-group extensions; related to relative/Malcev completions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hain (relative completion of SL2(Z), 1990s) for related completions; this specific computation is unattributed

ideas.what: Parametrization by the head ξ0 plus signs ε2, ε3, with recovery of μ when 2 is regular or invertible.
ideas.modern_name: explicit coordinates on a group scheme; bad-prime (2,3) behaviour

missed.claim: The structure of Σ_{ρ,σ} / Z_{ρσ} at the primes 2 and 3 is left only partially treated. At 2 there is the regularity/invertibility hypothesis; at 3 the Im = Ker identification implicitly needs 3 invertible. The integral (over Spec Z) structure of this automorphism group scheme is thus not settled.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a minor point. Integral models of automorphism and centralizer group schemes tied to SL2(Z) behave specially at 2 and 3, the primes dividing 12. A careful treatment would only matter to someone reconstructing Grothendieck's schematic Longue Marche programme.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a technical intermediate computation (choosing a basis of M_0 and eliminating variables) inside a larger unpublished project. The broader idea of a schematic, over-arbitrary-base treatment of automorphism groups of modular-group extensions is interesting and unpublished. This page itself contains no standalone new result.
transcription_corrections: 'ν0 ∈ Im(...)' in (136 bis) should read 'η0 ∈ Im(G_a → M_0)'.
'D*_12' should be 'O*_12' (same object as the O*_12 on the previous page).
In (139), '(μ, ξ0, β0) ↦ (μ, β0)' should be '(μ, ξ0, η0) ↦ (μ, η0)'; likewise 'les valeurs des η0' in the NB.
In (138), the underlined M_0 = Zδ × Z(3λ1) is meant as the vector group G_aδ × G_a(3λ1); the crossed-out symbol is 'Z̲'.
'dans si on connaît' should read 'donc si on connaît'.
'hyp. de 2 cut section régulière' should read 'hyp. de 2 est section régulière de O_S'.
'car ξ0 se récupère avec μ, η0 locaux [par] l'équation des têtes' rather than a garbled reading.
